summary: Initial H1-H7 scientific ledger published with predicted evidence and adversarial kill tests; wedge and crawl harnesses distinguished.
Initial metrics reframed the first axis as configuration rather than commit and measured bad runs whose committed virtual time raced far beyond wall time while guest progress froze.
Provisional root-cause verdict confirmed H1-H4 and initially killed controller-specific H6 after an apparent bare-QEMU wedge; this scope was later corrected by controlled socket A/B evidence.
Same-binary controls showed no-rcb alone and the full three-knob stack still boot bare busybox; the permanent wedge additionally required controller topology.

Controlled socket A/B confirmed H6: stdio and file-console variants booted, while adding serial and QMP listening sockets wedged at HPET. The earlier bare-wedge claim and STARVED-TAIL discriminator were retracted.
Lead-scientist adversarial sign-off accepted the corrected socket-trigger root cause and recorded the remaining turn-order and log-tooling gaps.
Investigation reopened after an external report attributed an approximately 20 percent residual rcb-time failure rate to PMU over-skid; primary evidence was not yet attached.
Captured logs contained zero PMU over-target lines; the observed signature was virtual-time skid from immediate SleepUntil(0) poll yields, with green 868 versus wedge approximately 817814.

The unverified PMU-skid label was retracted: the panic path was possible in source, but no demo5 log contained its signature; residual poller/vCPU starvation became leading but still required a clean rcb-time wedge witness.

details.required_next: per-run panic audit and fixed-input decision comparison

summary: Adversarial review found a cited 30.5M-turn witness had been overwritten and its recovered parse was unreliable. PMU-skid remained unsupported; poller-livelock was downgraded to leading but unproven for rcb-time; isolated N=30 experiments were launched.

details.new_experiment: private skidexp strict and target-timeslice arms

summary: First 33 isolated busybox boots were all green with zero skid panics and byte-identical deterministic columns across a twofold load swing; high SleepUntil(0) count alone did not predict a wedge.

Progress-based classification found busybox strict 7/7 green, byte-identical deterministic metrics and console output, zero PMU skid lines, and wall time 328-345s varying only with load; fixed wall timeouts had mislabeled slow progress as wedges.
Provisional batch verdict reported busybox 60/60 green and an apparent controller 16/16 failure with zero skid; the controller arm was later shown invalid because its timeout used virtualized time.

The controller 16/16 failure rate was invalidated: qemu_controller measured its internal timeout on racing virtual time, unlike production's outer wall-clock enforcement. The run still demonstrated vtime-skew but not production reliability.

PMU-skid was refuted only for valid busybox boots, not for controller plus rcb-time; prior independent evidence of one skid panic in five controller runs remained live. PMU robustness and poller-livelock were separated as orthogonal failure modes.

details.next: valid controller N>=20 with separate skid and livelock classification

summary: A valid controller plus rcb-time experiment was launched with an outer real-wall timeout, huge inner virtual timeout, private assets, and explicit skid, livelock, slow-censored, and other classifications.
Valid controller harness smoke reached QMP and HPET; process-group cleanup and committed-time fallback bugs were fixed before the N=20 batch.

First two valid controller runs both booted in approximately 527-529s with zero skid or livelock, confirming the earlier 16/16 failure was entirely a virtual-time timeout artifact and HPET was a slow crawl rather than a freeze.
PMU panic-then-wedge root cause localized: the per-tracee async task assert-panics after disabling the one-shot timer, leaving the tracee ptrace-stopped and bypassing cleanup and rearm.

details.nonfatal_fix: route actual late stop through Detcore accounting then normal rearm

summary: Valid controller batch reached 4/4 boot, zero skid and zero livelock; all runs ended at the same guest timestamp and SleepUntil(0) count despite host load 72-143, while wall time varied 527-543s.
Debug episode CLI and mutable hypothesis, evidence, and suspect snapshots were implemented in parent PR 25; demo5 state was migrated and 20 scheduler/time commits seeded as open suspects.

Prior wholesale Kendo-style argmin-vruntime design was recovered and remains invalidated: excluding poll retries freezes one minimum waiter; charging retries makes two pollers alternate while productive workers starve.

Forced zero-margin validation produced 469 consecutive over-skid events with advancing targets and clean exit, proving the new nonfatal late-event path rearms PMU alarms; old non-rearm applies only after fatal panic.

details.demo5_causality: not established without an over-skid witness

summary: Reverie PR 313 implemented typed over-skid handling, structured fatal cleanup, nonfatal late-event accounting and rearm, and raised the EPYC margin from 1000 to 66276 RCB.

Partial spin sweep captured 393.46s committed virtual time against 0.0797s guest progress in 90s wall, with 88.8 percent immediate polls and no preemption; healthy rcb-time runs continued preemption to the tail, arguing against rearm failure in successful boots.
Debug PR hygiene added ignore guards for raw logs, boot artifacts, VM images, kernels and archives while keeping JSON, Markdown and CSV investigation state trackable.

Scheduler design proposed bounded service-lead eligibility above existing priority and FIFO without argmin selection, poller identity inspection, or GlobalTime changes; it cannot repair a vCPU already blocked outside the run queue.

details.mechanism: threads at service lead >= B defer; existing order selects within eligible band
details.demo5_limit: wake/readmission still required for blocked dtid7

summary: Scheduler fairness and aging research artifact completed with prior-art recovery, literature survey, scored alternatives, runnable liveness argument, Demo5 limitations, and validation gates.

Append-only coordinator journal initialized with immutable sequence IDs, source-note provenance, stable hypothesis slugs, artifact pointers, and correction-by-supersession; coordinator owns only the history path while 237 owns CLI and schema integration.
Curated demo5 lab notebook was added to PR 25 with explored, invalidated, and frontier sections plus change-detection and notebook-sync support.
Episode hygiene tooling switched from blanket log ignores to ignored-first storage, per-episode ignore and VCS_MISSING manifests, and a size-blocking pre-commit backstop.
H8 was confirmed: no-rcb target-timeslice sweep was insensitive across four orders of magnitude, with flat virtual-time burn and zero preemptions; rcb-time control responded and preempted.

details.mechanism: approximately 74ms relative-timeout poll loop advances committed time without vCPU instruction progress

summary: Naive PMU rearm-failure signature was invalidated: preemption can cease during a healthy phase transition and later resume. H9 remained open and required a non-booting skid witness; H8 stayed confirmed.

details.counterexample: runs 15 and 16 booted; run 15 later resumed preemption

summary: Debug CLI, snapshots, curated notebook workflow, episode hygiene scaffolding, size hook, and suspect bootstrap were verified end-to-end on PR 25.
Valid rcb-time controller batch completed 18/20 boots plus two slow-censored runs, zero skid panics and zero livelocks; boot decisions were byte-identical across load.

Debug-infra PR fixed its episode-script portability findings and completed all requested snapshot, notebook, hygiene, and suspect-query components; unrelated main portability failures remained external blockers.
Fairness implementation proposed bounded per-thread service-lead eligibility behind a research flag, charging committed turns while preserving legacy priority and FIFO order within the eligible band.
Bounded service-lead overlay was implemented default-off, without clock changes, and passed eight runqueue unit tests plus formatting and lint checks.
Archaeology identified parent commit 0591104 as the demo flag flip: it added no-rcb-time and disabled max-timeslice 31 minutes after the known-good Hermit anchor.

Under short validation budgets, fairness failed across B=2..10000 and a trace appeared to show the vCPU blocked after a wake-before-wait sequence; this lost-wakeup root-cause claim was later superseded by longer-budget boots.
Draft PR 1386 published the default-off fairness overlay with honest disclosure that it had not met the demo5 success bar.
Adversarial review accepted the disabled path but found the enabled counter charged host-timing-dependent poll-retry commits, allowing external readiness to influence eligibility and real scheduling.

details.required_gate: make -j8 strict verify, at least five bitwise-identical runs

summary: Same-binary three-config test at Hermit 2a7ca98 confirmed historical green used armed PMU timing and the flipped no-rcb configuration produced zero preemptions and timeout; H10 was killed, H11 and S21 confirmed, S01-S20 cleared for the immediate cause.
Fairness PR documented the enabled-path determinism gate and a parent root-cause report recorded the provisional lost-futex-wakeup explanation; both demo attribution and report were later corrected.

Full-Linux HEAD with rcb-time restored timed out under a 180s budget while the last-good busybox evidence was green, motivating a post-breakage second-regression search; this initial result was budget-sensitive.
Initial endpoint comparison found adbfaca3 booting full-Linux in 103s while 2f3689bd timed out, provisionally supporting a second code regression after the config flip.
First post-breakage bisect was invalidated when it landed on inert test-harness commit e8c2f704 whose binary was byte-identical to its good parent but classified differently.

Provisional no-second-regressor verdict attributed green versus timeout to host timing after the same anchor binary timed out 5/5 under load; later controlled and multisect evidence reopened this conclusion.

Commit archaeology recovered the flip rationale: 0591104 disabled PMU timing to avoid hardware-skid perturbations, asserting the syscall-rich workload did not need PMU preemption; no committed full-Linux validation evidence accompanied the flip.

details.readme_rationale: scheduler check-ins suffice; avoid PMU skid perturbing timing logs

summary: Taskset-isolated matched comparison provisionally restored a categorical endpoint split, reopening the second-regression hypothesis: adbfaca3 4/4 green versus HEAD 0/3.

Updated short-budget evidence again attributed the apparent wedge to a wake-before-wait futex sequence outside the runnable queue and kept fairness as a default-off research artifact; this attribution was later falsified.

Sticky pending-wake prototype was active but still timed out under short budgets, falsifying the single lost-wakeup explanation and provisionally shifting attribution to userspace mutex and unproductive poller behavior; this too was later superseded by adequate-budget boots.

Isolated bisect again landed on a docs-only commit e3067d69 with a binary identical to its parent but opposite classifications; six reruns flipped it back green, so no discrete boundary was accepted at this stage.
Cgroup-boxed multisect measured commit 1663138d at 0/6 green under matched RCB-on configuration, with early QMP-socket starvation and 76k-105k immediate polls.
Matched-load boxed multisect found a provisional green-rate step at 1663138d: earlier anchors 6/6 and 5/6 versus 1663138d and later commits 0/6; decisive HEAD-with-revert interleaving was launched.

Adequate 600s validation retracted the fairness-task wedge premise: shipped rcb-armed demo5 booted 6/6 in 238-248s; all earlier 90-200s fairness, lost-wake, and sticky-wake failures killed a normal approximately 90s HPET pause before later progress.

details.conclusion: slow load-sensitive crawl, no demonstrated livelock on this host

summary: PR 25 refreshed the mutable episode snapshot through H11, E22, and S21: S01-S20 cleared and parent config flip 0591104 confirmed as the immediate regressor.

Load-controlled band-rotated A/B/C/D refuted 1663138d as the second regressor: the commit booted 3/3 while HEAD with it reverted still timed out 3/3. Search moved later toward the guest-clock committed-time cluster.

details.head: timeout
details.confirmation: held until host load below approximately 90

summary: Source audit killed the proposed 1663138d clone-priority mechanism: it retimes parent SIGCHLD admission but does not change child versus parent priority, and demo5 boot does not traverse that make-jobserver path.

details.behavioral_change: defer and readmit parent SIGCHLD at non-poller quiescence

summary: The requested 1663138d second-bug deep dive was redirected into a falsification report rather than inventing lost-wakeup causality.

At extreme 2.6-2.8x oversubscription a 700s run timed out at the normal HPET crawl with QMP present; fair-share time matched the approximately 243s low-load boot, so this was load dilation rather than a distinct wedge.

details.conclusion: no valid genuine load-induced wedge evidence at HEAD

summary: Phase-1 machine-readable compatibility scorecard was pushed with separate Hermit and Reverie tables; the stressed shared-primary rerun was discarded and future expansion remains boxed and quiet-host gated.
